references.text: As part of the blessings for obedience, God promises Israel that their seed will yield a plentiful harvest, reflecting the promise of fruitfulness in Mark 4:8.
Moses reminds the people of Israel how God blessed their work and crops in the promised land, paralleling the good soil that yields a plentiful harvest in Mark 4:8.
Isaiah uses the image of rain bringing fertility to the earth as an analogy for God's word accomplishing what it was sent to do, similar to how seed sown in good soil bears fruit in Mark 4:8.
Hosea urges Israel to sow righteousness and reap love, which can be seen as a spiritual parallel to the physical fruitfulness of the seed in Mark 4:8.
Paul warns that whatever one sows, they will also reap, whether it is for the spirit or for the flesh, reflecting the principle of sowing and reaping found in Mark 4:8.
